{{NSE|EDELWEISS}} | subsidiaries = {{Unbulleted list||Edelweiss Life Insurance Company Limited|Edelweiss Asset Reconstruction Limited|EAAA India Limited|Edelweiss Asset Management Limiter|ECL Finance Limited|Edelweiss Retail Finance Limited}} | website = {{URL|edelweissfin.com}} }} '''Edelweiss Group''' (officially known as '''Edelweiss Financial Services Limited''') is an [[investment]] and [[financial services]] company based in [[Mumbai]].{{cite news|title=How Edelweiss built a business for the long run {{!}} Forbes India|url=http://forbesindia.com/article/boardroom/how-edelweiss-built-a-business-for-the-long-run/39907/1|work=Forbes India}} It was co-founded by [[Rashesh Shah]] and Venkat Ramaswamy. The company deals in various financial services ranging from brokerage services to life insurance and [[general insurance]], private equity and other investment-related services through subsidiaries.{{Cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/magazines/panache/edelweiss-chairman-rashesh-shahs-advice-to-entrepreneurs-give-up-the-startup-energy-to-scale-up/articleshow/61764447.cms|title=Economic Times|date=23 November 2017|website=Economic Times|last1=Menon|first1=Rashmi}} It has a network of sub-brokers and authorised people across India. It is registered with [[National Stock Exchange of India|National Stock Exchange]] of India, [[Bombay Stock Exchange]] and [[Multi Commodity Exchange]]. ==History== Edelweiss was founded in 1995 by Rashesh Shah and Venkat Ramaswamy.{{cite news|last1=Sinha|first1=Shilpy|title=What makes investors trust their money with these 5 financial supermarkets of India | url = https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/company/corporate-trends/what-makes-investors-trust-their-money-with-these-5-financial-supermarkets-of-india/articleshow/54321160.cms |website = The Economic Times |access-date=22 January 2018 |date=14 September 2016}} Initially, the company worked on private equity syndication, mergers, acquisitions (M&A) and focused on advisory services.{{cite web|title=Rashesh Shah: Every setback is an opportunity to recalibrate {{!}} Forbes India|url=http://www.forbesindia.com/article/fourth-anniversary-special/rashesh-shah-every-setback-is-an-opportunity-to-recalibrate/35347/1|website=Forbes India}} Edelweiss worked on mergers & acquisitions, providing advisory and investment banking services.{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Company Profile for ${Instrument_CompanyName} |url=https://in.reuters.com/finance/stocks/company-profile/EDEL.BO |access-date=2019-03-26 |website=IN |language=en}} Edelweiss also offered equity broking, portfolio management, and wholesale financing services to individuals and corporates.{{Cite web|url=https://www.ndtv.com/business/stock/edelweiss-financial-services-ltd_edelweiss/reports|title=Edelweiss Financial: Reports, Company History, Directors Report, Chairman's Speech, Auditors Report of Edelweiss Financial - NDTV|website=www.ndtv.com|access-date=2019-03-26}} === 1996–2004 === The company became a merchant bank in 2000.{{Cite web|url=http://www.forbesindia.com/printcontent/35347|title=Forbes India Magazine - Print|website=www.forbesindia.com|access-date=2019-03-26}} It was also helped start-ups raise funds via the non-IPO route, [[Venture capital|Venture Capital (VC)]] and [[Private equity fund|Private Equity funds]] (PE). In 2000, the company had capital mark of {{INR}}50 million. It acquired Rooshnil Securities in 2001.{{cite news|last1=Sultana|first1=Nasrin|title=Edelweiss Group acquires Religare's securities business|url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/z0VexoFcHq9COV4NjPfSQO/Edelweiss-acquires-Religares-securities-business.html|work=Livemint.com|date=20 December 2017}} === 2004–2012 === During this period Edelweiss added institutional broking and [[Non-bank financial institution|non-banking financial company (NBFC)]] activity to its portfolio. In 2007, Edelweiss obtained its Clearing Member License.{{Cite web|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/edelweiss-financial-services-ltd/infocompanyhistory/companyid-19100.cms|title=Edelweiss Financial Services History {{!}} Edelweiss Financial Services Information - The Economic Times|website=economictimes.indiatimes.com|access-date=2019-03-26}} The same year, Edelweiss commenced asset management business with the launch of real estate funds. In 2007, Edelweiss Global Wealth Management was established to offer wealth structuring solutions,{{buzzword inline|date=September 2019}} asset protection, asset transfer strategies, risk management and investment banking solutions.{{buzzword inline|date=September 2019}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.ndtv.com/business/stock/edelweiss-financial-services-ltd_edelweiss/reports|title=Edelweiss Financial: Reports, Company History, Directors Report, Chairman's Speech, Auditors Report of Edelweiss Financial - NDTVProfit.com|website=www.ndtv.com|access-date=2019-03-26}} In 2008, EdelGive Foundation (the company's charitable wing) was established with education and livelihoods as its primary focus areas.{{Cite web|url=https://educationinnovations.org/funder/edelgive-foundation|title=EdelGive Foundation {{!}} Center for Education Innovations|website=educationinnovations.org|access-date=2019-03-26|archive-date=20 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181120135858/https://educationinnovations.org/funder/edelgive-foundation|url-status=dead}} In mid-2008, with the launch of its wholly owned subsidiary, Edelweiss Alternative Asset Advisors Limited (EAAA), it entered the alternative asset management market. The group developed the platform organically, focusing on private credit, real estate, and infrastructure yield strategies for institutional and high-net-worth investors. In 2010, Edelweiss acquired Anagram Capital, for Rs. 164 crore.{{Cite news|url=https://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-business/Edelweiss-to-acquire-Anagram-Capital/article15969902.ece|title=Edelweiss to acquire Anagram Capital|date=2010-01-28|work=The Hindu|access-date=2019-03-26|language=en-IN|issn=0971-751X}} In 2011, Edelweiss Tokio Life Insurance was established as a joint venture between Edelweiss and Japanese insurer [[Tokio Marine]]. Edelweiss held a 74 per cent stake in the JV.{{Cite news|url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/companies/Edelweiss-inks-joint-venture-agreement-with-Tokio-Marine/article16893709.ece|title=Edelweiss inks joint venture agreement with Tokio Marine|date=2009-11-23|work=The Hindu|access-date=2019-03-26|agency=PTI|language=en-IN|issn=0971-751X}} === 2012–2022 === In 2014, Edelweiss Financial Services acquired Mumbai-based asset management company, Forefront Capital Management.{{Cite news|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/edelweiss-fin-services-acquires-forefront-capital-management-114050100262_1.html|title=Edelweiss Fin Services acquires Forefront Capital Management|last=Reporter|first=B. S.|date=2014-05-01|work=Business Standard India|access-date=2019-03-26}} In 2016, Edelweiss Asset Management Company completed the acquisition of fund schemes of JP Morgan Asset Management India.{{Cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/wealth/mutual-funds/edelweiss-asset-management-to-acquire-jp-morgans-mutual-fund/articleshow/51513625.cms|title=Edelweiss Asset Management to acquire JP Morgan's Mutual Fund|date=2016-04-04|work=The Economic Times|access-date=2019-03-26}} In September 2016, Edelweiss Financial Services Ltd also agreed to acquire Ambit Investment Advisors' longshot hedge fund Ambit Alpha Fund.{{Cite web|url=http://www.forbesindia.com/article/special/edelweiss-financial-acquires-ambit-alpha-fund/44365/1|title=Edelweiss Financial acquires Ambit Alpha Fund|website=Forbes India|language=en|access-date=2019-03-26}} In 2016, [[Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec]] (CDPQ), a pension fund manager in North America, acquired 20 per cent equity stake in Edelweiss Asset Reconstruction Company (EARC) with a view to investing annually in stressed assets and the specialized corporate credit segment, over a four-year period.{{Cite web|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/money-and-banking/canadas-cdpq-to-pick-up-20-stake-in-edelweiss-arc/article9179451.ece|title=Canada's CDPQ to pick up 20% stake in Edelweiss ARC|website=@businessline|date=3 October 2016 |language=en|access-date=2019-03-26}} In 2022, Edelweiss General Insurance's Group Health Policy includes LGBTQ+ community.{{cite news |last1=Standard |first1=Business |title=Edelweiss |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/pf/edelweiss-general-insurance-s-group-health-policy-includes-lgbtq-community-122091000221_1.html}} === 2023–present === In 2023, the group launched its first dedicated Climate Fund, targeting a total corpus of US$500 million. The fund focuses on [[climate change mitigation]] and adaptation investments across sectors such as renewable energy, electric mobility, green infrastructure, water treatment, and industrial decarbonization. With a fund tenure of 10–12 years, it is structured to provide long-term capital to projects aligned with India's net-zero goals and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. {{Cite web |title=EDELWEISS CLIMATE FUND |url=https://www.eib.org/en/projects/pipelines/all/20230048 |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=www.eib.org}} In 2024, the Reserve Bank of India suspended Edelweiss Asset Reconstruction Company from acquiring more business, and placed restrictions on the business activities of ECL Finance on concerns of [[evergreening]] of loans. Both are subsidiaries of Edelweiss Financial Services Ltd.{{cite news |title=RBI bars Edelweiss ARC from acquiring financial asset with immediate effect |url=https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/rbi-bars-edelweiss-arc-from-acquiring-financial-asset-with-immediate-effect-124052901380_1.html |publisher=Business Standard}} In December 2024, Edelweiss Alternatives filed a draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for an initial public offering. The filing was rejected by SEBI in March 2025, citing regulatory concerns. The episode drew media attention due to the nature of the intervention and the company's prominent position in the alternatives space. In July 2025, Nuvama Wealth Management, a firm spun off from Edelweiss Financial Services, was subjected to an income tax search by Indian authorities in connection with alleged irregularities. While Nuvama operates as an independent entity, Edelweiss Financial Services retains a small residual stake through its financial subsidiaries.{{cite news |last=Kumar |first=Shivendra |title=Nuvama shares fall 4% on reports of income tax search in connection to Jane Street case |newspaper=The Economic Times |date=31 July 2025 |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/it-raids-nuvama-wealth-formerly-edelweiss-broking/articleshow/123015976.cms |access-date=31 July 2025}}{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=waUhAupgah8 |title=Edelweiss Financial Services: Public Analysis of Risk Patterns & Regulatory History |date=2025-10-06 |last=Whistleblower |access-date=2025-10-06 |via=YouTube}} In September 2025, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) settled adjudication proceedings against two entities of Edelweiss Alternatives namely Edelweiss Stressed and Troubled Assets Revival Fund Trust (ESTAR) and its investment manager, Edelweiss Alternative Asset Advisors Ltd (EAAAL), over alleged violations of the Alternative Investment Funds (AIF) Regulations. The case arose from investor complaints filed on SEBI's SCORES platform in 2021-22 and a subsequent show-cause notice issued in July 2024, citing governance and disclosure lapses. According to SEBI's settlement order dated 30 September 2025, the entities jointly paid a settlement amount of ₹61.42 lakh, and certain officers-in-default accepted a 12-month bar from associating with the firms in any capacity. SEBI stated that the settlement was made “without admission or denial” of findings and that the regulator may reopen the case if disclosures are later found to be incomplete or misleading.{{Cite web |title=SEBI {{!}} Settlement Order in the matter of examination of SCORES complaints against Edelweiss Stressed and Troubled Assets Revival Fund Trust |url=https://www.sebi.gov.in/enforcement/orders/sep-2025/settlement-order-in-the-matter-of-examination-of-scores-complaints-against-edelweiss-stressed-and-troubled-assets-revival-fund-trust_96988.html |access-date=2025-10-16 |website=www.sebi.gov.in}} ==See also== * [[Edelweiss Broking Limited]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== * {{Official website|https://www.edelweissfin.com/}} * [https://www.hizuno.com/ Zuno Insurance] [[Category:Asset management companies]] [[Category:Financial services companies based in Mumbai]] [[Category:Brokerage firms]] [[Category:Mutual funds of India]] [[Category:Exchange-traded funds]] [[Category:Investment management companies of India]] [[Category:Indian companies established in 1995]] [[Category:1995 establishments in Maharashtra]] [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange]]
extract:
Edelweiss Group (officially known as Edelweiss Financial Services Limited) is an investment and financial services company based in Mumbai. It was co-founded by Rashesh Shah and  Venkat Ramaswamy.
The company deals in various financial services ranging from brokerage services to life insurance and general insurance, private equity and other investment-related services through subsidiaries. It has a network of sub-brokers and authorised people across India. It is registered with National Stock Exchange of India, Bombay Stock Exchange and Multi Commodity Exchange.
